## Prompts

The conversation was in Traditional Chinese.

1. > 接著幫我依照他的風格完成第四張圖
>
>    *(Now complete the fourth chart, following her style.)*
>
>    Context supplied beforehand: the assignment PDF, my teammate's published
>    page, and read access to the cloned repository — in particular `Chart3.R`,
>    `assign04.qmd`, and `data/hpi_clean.csv`.

2. > 幫我看一下
>
>    *(Take a look at this.)* — sent with the first rendered PNG, asking for a
>    review against the other three charts.

## What I Had to Fix

- **The y-axis title came out horizontal.** `theme_hackathon()` re-declares
  `axis.title.y` through `%+replace%` without an `angle`, so the angle resets to
  zero and the panel is squeezed. I caught it by comparing the first render
  against Chart 1, where the same fix already appears. Commit `07f074f`.
- **The first draft of the commit would have touched the whole repository.**
  The clone is on Windows, so every text file showed as modified on line endings
  alone — 13,521 insertions and 13,527 deletions across 52 files, all whitespace.
  I staged only the four new paths instead of `git add -A`.
- **`source("R/theme.R")` pointed at a file that was not in the repository.**
  `Chart1.R` and `Chart3.R` both call it, but the theme existed only inside the
  setup chunk of the Quarto document, so those scripts failed from a clean R
  session. Extracting it fixed a checklist item for the whole team, not just my
  chart.

## Design Decisions That Are Mine

- Sorting the continents by mean HPI rather than alphabetically, so the chart
  answers its own title.
- Printing `n =` inside each column. Oceania's mean rests on four countries and
  Asia's on seventeen; without the counts the five columns read as equally
  reliable.
- Stating in the subtitle that the mean is **unweighted**, since Chart 1 uses a
  population-weighted mean and the two numbers would otherwise appear to disagree.
